name: Aster recovery, hooks and rollout contracts
description: Fixed synthetic action sequences with common goal checks across ablation arms. These are mechanism checks, not autonomous model tasks. Before-hook ablation disables only that lifecycle boundary; sandbox and permission policies stay active.

cases.description: Two identical successful searches trigger repeated_identical independently of read_file.
Two identical directory listings trigger repeated_identical even when output is a list of paths.
After a fresh read, repeating the same nonmatching patch produces an identical blocked result and triggers recovery.
Alternating two invalid patch strategies with zero and two matches forms ABAB; differing error contents do not hide oscillation.
Three different old_text arguments each yield patch_nonunique with zero occurrences; the shared failed result triggers output_loop.
Equal empty outputs from three different successful searches are not a failed-output loop.
A real edit clears the stall window; rereading the edited file is necessary fresh evidence.
A real write elsewhere clears previous observations even when the next read has exactly the same arguments and output as an earlier read.
Writing identical bytes is not a changed_path; read/write/read/write remains an ABAB loop and must stop without budget.
The same two-loop sequence requires two recovery interventions; compare budgets zero, one and two with the same completion goal.
After spending two recoveries a third independent repeat terminates the run; increasing the budget to three permits the scripted continuation.
Checkpoint/resume preserves an untriggered one-read window; the same next read triggers recovery rather than starting a fresh window.
Checkpoint/resume after ABA preserves enough history for the next B to trigger oscillation.
Once stall recovery is exhausted, subsequent scripted tool calls and finalization must not execute a write or revive the terminal run.
Starting a new task clears an untriggered read window; its first identical read cannot inherit a false repeat from the prior task.
A real write clears detection history but must not replenish the per-run recovery allowance; the next repeated read exhausts it.

detector_contracts.description: JSON object key order is irrelevant to an identical call.
New call ids, timing and evidence metadata do not constitute new information.
Changing visible content for the same call is not repetition.
A transition from blocked to success is not an identical outcome.
Different failure reasons break equality even when the visible error body is unchanged.
Different tool names remain different calls even with equal arguments and successful output.
The shared failed-output rule crosses tool names after three identical status/reason/content results.
A partially successful operation with real changed_paths clears stale history even when its overall status is an error.
Current ceiling: omitted and explicit default arguments are distinct raw keys; the detector does not perform schema normalization.
Current ceiling: ABCABC is outside the adjacent-repeat/ABAB heuristics and must not be reported as detected coverage.
